In [[mathematics]], the '''Gauss–Kuzmin distribution''' is a [[discrete probability distribution]] that arises as the limit [[probability distribution]] of the coefficients in the [[continued fraction]] expansion of a [[random variable]] [[uniform distribution (continuous)|uniformly distributed]] in (0,&nbsp;1).<ref>{{MathWorld |title=Gauss–Kuzmin Distribution |urlname=Gauss-KuzminDistribution}}</ref> The distribution is named after [[Carl Friedrich Gauss]], who derived it around 1800,<ref>{{cite book |last=Gauss |first=Johann Carl Friedrich |author-link=Johann Carl Friedrich Gauss |url=http://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/dms/load/img/?PPN=PPN236018647 |pages=552–556 |title=Werke Sammlung |volume=10/1}}</ref> and [[Rodion Kuzmin]], who gave a bound on the rate of convergence in 1929.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Kuzmin |first=R. O. |title=On a problem of Gauss |journal=Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR |date=1928 |pages=375–380}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |first=R. O. |last=Kuzmin |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1928.6/ICM1928.6.ocr.pdf |title=Sur un probleme de Gauss
|journal=Atti del Congresso Internazionale dei Matematici, Bologna |date=1932 |volume=6 |pages=83–89}}</ref> It is given by the [[probability mass function]]

: <math> p(k) = - \log_2 \left( 1 - \frac{1}{(k+1)^2}\right)~.</math>

==Gauss&ndash;Kuzmin theorem==

Let

:<math> x = \cfrac{1}{k_1 + \cfrac{1}{k_2 + \cdots}} </math>

be the continued fraction expansion of a number ''x'' uniformly distributed in (0,&nbsp;1). Then

:<math> \lim_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{P} \left\{ k_n = k \right\} = - \log_2\left(1 - \frac{1}{(k+1)^2}\right)~.</math>

Equivalently, let

:<math> x_n = \cfrac{1}{k_{n+1} + \cfrac{1}{k_{n+2} + \cdots}}~; </math>

then

:<math> \Delta_n(s) = \mathbb{P} \left\{ x_n \leq s \right\} - \log_2(1+s) </math>

tends to zero as ''n'' tends to infinity.

==Rate of convergence==

In 1928, Kuzmin gave the bound

:<math> |\Delta_n(s)| \leq C \exp(-\alpha \sqrt{n})~. </math>

In 1929, [[Paul Lévy (mathematician)|Paul Lévy]]<ref>{{cite journal |last=Lévy |first=P. |title=Sur les lois de probabilité dont dépendant les quotients complets et incomplets d'une fraction continue |journal=[[Bulletin de la Société Mathématique de France]] |date=1929 |volume=57 |pages=178–194 |doi=10.24033/bsmf.1150 |url=http://www.numdam.org/item?id=BSMF_1929__57__178_0 |jfm=55.0916.02|doi-access=free }}</ref> improved it to

:<math> |\Delta_n(s)| \leq C \, 0.7^n~. </math>

Later, [[Eduard Wirsing]] showed<ref>{{cite journal |last=Wirsing |first=E. |title=On the theorem of Gauss–Kusmin–Lévy and a Frobenius-type theorem for function spaces |journal=Acta Arithmetica |date=1974 |volume=24 |issue=5 |pages=507–528|doi=10.4064/aa-24-5-507-528 |doi-access=free }}</ref> that, for ''λ''&nbsp;=&nbsp;0.30366... (the [[Gauss–Kuzmin–Wirsing constant]]), the limit

:<math> \Psi(s) = \lim_{n \to \infty} \frac{\Delta_n(s)}{(-\lambda)^n} </math>

exists for every ''s'' in [0,&nbsp;1], and the function ''Ψ''(''s'') is analytic and satisfies ''Ψ''(0)&nbsp;=&nbsp;''Ψ''(1)&nbsp;=&nbsp;0. Further bounds were proved by [[K. I. Babenko]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Babenko |first=K. I. |title=On a problem of Gauss |journal=Soviet Math. Dokl. |date=1978 |volume=19 |pages=136–140}}</ref>
